    out["okres_tokens"] = out["okres_all"].map(okres_tokens)
    out["okres_now"] = out["okres_tokens"].map(lambda t: t[-1] if t else None)
    out["in_1910"] = out["okres_id"].notna() & out["status_1910"].notna()

    seats: set[tuple[int, str]] = set()
    out["okres_1910_cs"] = out["okres_1910"]
    if districts is not None:
        codes = districts["okres_code"].str.split("-", expand=True).astype(int)
        okres_id = codes[0] * 1000 + codes[1]
        names = dict(zip(okres_id, districts["okres_cs"]))
        out["okres_1910_cs"] = out["okres_id"].map(names).fillna(out["okres_1910"])
        seats = set(zip(okres_id, districts["gerichtsbezirk_cs"].map(normalise_name)))

    is_seat = pd.Series([(o, n) in seats for o, n in zip(out["okres_id"], out["name_key"])],
                        index=out.index)
    commune = out["status_1910"].eq("obec")
    out["size_class"] = pd.Series("3 hamlet / part", index=out.index, dtype=object)
    out.loc[commune, "size_class"] = "2 other commune"
    out.loc[commune & is_seat, "size_class"] = "1 court-seat town"
    out.loc[~out["in_1910"], "size_class"] = None
    if "population_1910" in out.columns:
        out["size_class"] = pd.cut(out["population_1910"], POPULATION_BANDS,
                                   labels=POPULATION_LABELS, right=False).astype(object)
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The join
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_TYPE_PREFERENCE = {"Obec": {"obec": 0}, "Místní část": {"osada": 0, "cast": 0},
                    "Část": {"osada": 0, "cast": 0}}


def _type_penalty(place_type, status) -> int:
    """0 where the place's type and the settlement's 1910 status agree, else 1."""
    return _TYPE_PREFERENCE.get(place_type, {}).get(status, 1)


def join_places_to_settlements(
    places: pd.DataFrame,
    settlements: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    max_km: float = 5.0,
    fuzzy_km: float = 2.0,
    min_similarity: float = 85.0,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tie each database place to at most one 1910 settlement, by distance with a name check.

    Args:
        places: the scraper's places table (``geo_id, name, type, lat, lon, okres``).
        settlements: :func:`settlement_frame` output.
        max_km: furthest an exact-name pair may be apart.
        fuzzy_km: furthest a near-name pair may be apart.
        min_similarity: rapidfuzz ratio (0–100) on the normalised, de-accented names.

    Returns:
        One row per place — ``geo_id, settlement_row, match_method, distance_km,
        name_similarity`` — with ``settlement_row`` missing where nothing matched and
        ``match_method`` saying why (``unmatched: no such name`` / ``… too far`` /
        ``… ambiguous``).  Asserted: one row per place, no settlement used twice.
    """
    P = places[["geo_id", "name", "type", "lat", "lon", "okres"]].copy()
    P["name_key"] = P["name"].map(normalise_name)
    S = settlements[["settlement_row", "name_key", "status_1910", "lat", "lon", "okres_tokens"]]
    # a city part is reachable under its own name as well as under "CITY IV-PART"
    alt = settlements.loc[settlements["name_key_alt"].notna(), S.columns.drop("name_key")].assign(
        name_key=settlements["name_key_alt"].dropna())
    by_name = pd.concat([S, alt[S.columns]], ignore_index=True)

    pairs = P.merge(by_name, on="name_key", suffixes=("", "_s"))
    pairs = pairs[pairs["name_key"] != ""]
    geocoded = pairs["lat_s"].notna()
    pairs["distance_km"] = np.where(
        geocoded, haversine_km(pairs["lat"], pairs["lon"], pairs["lat_s"].fillna(0),
                               pairs["lon_s"].fillna(0)), np.nan)
    pairs["okres_ok"] = [o in toks for o, toks in zip(pairs["okres"], pairs["okres_tokens"])]
    pairs["penalty"] = [_type_penalty(t, s) for t, s in zip(pairs["type"], pairs["status_1910"])]

    used_places: dict[int, tuple] = {}
    used_settlements: set[int] = set()

    def accept(geo_id, row, method, km, similarity) -> None:
        used_places[int(geo_id)] = (int(row), method, km, similarity)
        used_settlements.add(int(row))

    # tier 1 — exact name, both geocoded, close: nearest pair first
    near = pairs[geocoded & (pairs["distance_km"] <= max_km)].sort_values(["distance_km", "penalty"])
    for r in near.itertuples():
        if r.geo_id not in used_places and r.settlement_row not in used_settlements:
            accept(r.geo_id, r.settlement_row, "name+coords", round(float(r.distance_km), 2), 100.0)

    # tier 2 — exact name, settlement not geocoded, okres on its timeline, unique both ways
    loose = pairs[~geocoded & pairs["okres_ok"]
                  & ~pairs["geo_id"].isin(list(used_places))
                  & ~pairs["settlement_row"].isin(used_settlements)]
    loose = loose[loose["penalty"] == loose.groupby("geo_id")["penalty"].transform("min")]
    n_for_place = loose.groupby("geo_id")["settlement_row"].transform("nunique")
    n_for_settlement = loose.groupby("settlement_row")["geo_id"].transform("nunique")
    ambiguous = set(loose.loc[(n_for_place > 1) | (n_for_settlement > 1), "geo_id"])
    for r in loose[(n_for_place == 1) & (n_for_settlement == 1)].itertuples():
        accept(r.geo_id, r.settlement_row, "name+okres", np.nan, 100.0)

    # tier 3 — near-identical name, very close
    left = P[~P["geo_id"].isin(list(used_places)) & P["lat"].notna() & (P["name_key"] != "")]
    right = S[~S["settlement_row"].isin(used_settlements) & S["lat"].notna()]
    fuzzy_rows = []
    if len(left) and len(right):
        right_lat, right_lon = right["lat"].to_numpy(), right["lon"].to_numpy()
        right_keys = right["name_key"].map(strip_diacritics).to_numpy()
        right_ids = right["settlement_row"].to_numpy()
        for p in left.itertuples():
            km = haversine_km(p.lat, p.lon, right_lat, right_lon)
            key = strip_diacritics(p.name_key)
            for j in np.flatnonzero(km <= fuzzy_km):
                similarity = fuzz.ratio(key, right_keys[j])
                if similarity >= min_similarity:
                    fuzzy_rows.append((float(km[j]), -similarity, p.geo_id, right_ids[j]))
    for km, neg_similarity, geo_id, row in sorted(fuzzy_rows):
        if geo_id not in used_places and row not in used_settlements:
            accept(geo_id, row, "fuzzy+coords", round(km, 2), float(-neg_similarity))

    # why the rest did not match
    has_name = set(pairs["geo_id"])
    too_far = set(pairs.loc[geocoded & (pairs["distance_km"] > max_km), "geo_id"])
    rows = []
    for geo_id in P["geo_id"]:
        if int(geo_id) in used_places:
            rows.append((geo_id, *used_places[int(geo_id)]))
            continue
        reason = ("unmatched: ambiguous" if geo_id in ambiguous
                  else "unmatched: too far" if geo_id in too_far
                  else "unmatched: name elsewhere" if geo_id in has_name
                  else "unmatched: no such name")
        rows.append((geo_id, pd.NA, reason, np.nan, np.nan))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["geo_id", "settlement_row", "match_method",
                                      "distance_km", "name_similarity"])
    out["settlement_row"] = out["settlement_row"].astype("Int64")

    assert len(out) == len(places) and out["geo_id"].is_unique, "join: not one row per place"
    assert not out["settlement_row"].dropna().duplicated().any(), "join: a settlement matched twice"
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dates
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_SPAN_OF = {"year": 0, "decade": 9, "century": 99}


def starts_before(year, precision, cutoff: int = PRE_WAR_CUTOFF) -> str:
    """Does a (possibly fuzzy) year fall before ``cutoff``?  ``yes / no / ambiguous / unknown``."""
    if precision not in _SPAN_OF or pd.isna(year):
        return "unknown"
    earliest, latest = int(year), int(year) + _SPAN_OF[precision]
    if latest < cutoff:
        return "yes"
    if earliest >= cutoff:
        return "no"
    return "ambiguous"


_PERIOD_EDGES = [0, 1800, 1850, 1870, 1880, 1890, 1900, 1910, PRE_WAR_CUTOFF, 1920, 1950, 9999]
_PERIOD_LABELS = ["<1800", "1800–49", "1850–69", "1870s", "1880s", "1890s", "1900s",
                  "1910–13", "1914–19", "1920–49", "1950+"]
PERIOD_ORDER = _PERIOD_LABELS + ["191x (decade only)", "century only", "not recorded"]


def first_record_period(year, precision) -> str:
    """The period a place's first report falls in, for the distribution table.

    An exact year goes to its bin.  A decade does too, except ``191x`` — the one decade
    the 1914 line cuts — which is shown as its own row rather than assigned to a side.
    """
    if pd.isna(year) or precision not in _SPAN_OF:
        return "not recorded"
    if precision == "century":
        return "century only"
    if precision == "decade" and int(year) == 1910:
        return "191x (decade only)"
    return _PERIOD_LABELS[int(np.searchsorted(_PERIOD_EDGES, int(year), side="right")) - 1]


def place_dates(places: pd.DataFrame, ensembles: pd.DataFrame,
                cutoff: int = PRE_WAR_CUTOFF) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per place: how many ensembles, and whether theatre is recorded before ``cutoff``.

    ``ensemble_pre`` is True when at least one ensemble certainly starts before the
    cutoff; ``ensemble_ambiguous`` when none certainly does but one may (``191x``);
    ``first_record_pre`` reads the place page's own 'První zpráva'.  Key ``geo_id``.
    """
    E = ensembles.copy()
    E["pre"] = [starts_before(y, p, cutoff) for y, p in zip(E["year_from"], E["year_from_precision"])]
    per_place = E.groupby("geo_id").agg(
        n_ensembles=("ensemble_id", "size"),
        n_pre=("pre", lambda s: int((s == "yes").sum())),
        n_ambiguous=("pre", lambda s: int((s == "ambiguous").sum())),
        n_undated=("pre", lambda s: int((s == "unknown").sum())),
    )
    out = places[["geo_id"]].merge(per_place, on="geo_id", how="left", validate="1:1")
    counts = ["n_ensembles", "n_pre", "n_ambiguous", "n_undated"]
    out[counts] = out[counts].fillna(0).astype(int)
    out["ensemble_pre"] = out["n_pre"] > 0
    out["ensemble_ambiguous"] = (out["n_pre"] == 0) & (out["n_ambiguous"] > 0)
    first = [starts_before(y, p, cutoff) for y, p in
             zip(places["first_record_year"], places["first_record_precision"])]
    out["first_record_pre"] = [f == "yes" for f in first]
    out["first_record_known"] = [f != "unknown" for f in first]
    assert len(out) == len(places)
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What kind of association an ensemble's name points to
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Word-anchored on both sides, with the inflected forms listed: `sokol` must not fire
# inside the town of Sokolov, nor `orel` inside a longer word.  An *Osvětová beseda* is the
# post-1945 state cultural club, not the nineteenth-century reading society, and is left out.
# The first five are the pilot's; the rest were added for the chronicle (0.2.0), from the
# words commonest in its pre-1914 lines that none of the five matched.  "Divadelní spolek"
# is the free-standing amateur dramatic society (SDO, *ochotnická jednota*) — a society of
# its own, not a section of another, so a bare `DS`/`DrO` (which is usually "DS Sokola")
# is not it.  The database's abbreviations are read from its own key
# (``data/raw/theatre/abbreviations.csv``, 0.3.0) and matched **case-sensitively**, so
# `OS` is the *ochotnický spolek* and not the Czech word: SDO, OS, OJ, DJ, JDO, KrDO are
# free-standing dramatic societies; ČOS, ČOJ, ČOB the reading-and-dramatic society
# (*čtenářsko ochotnický spolek / jednota / beseda*), ČOB a beseda too; ČB the Česká
# beseda; NJ, NJS, NJP the national unions.  `ČOS` has a second reading in the key, the
# Sokol union (*Česká / Československá obec sokolská*), so a line naming it is also
# flagged (:data:`AMBIGUOUS_ABBREVIATIONS`).  `DS` (*soubor – skupina – spolek*) and `OB`
# (the post-1945 *osvětová beseda*) stay unread.
ASSOCIATION_PATTERNS: dict[str, re.Pattern] = {
    "Sokol": re.compile(
        r"\bsokol(?:a|u|e|em|ů|ové|sk[áéýou]\w*|stv\w*|ík\w*)?\b", re.I),
    "Hasiči": re.compile(
        r"\bhasič\w*|\bSDH\b", re.I),
    "Beseda": re.compile(
        r"(?<!osvětová\s)(?<!osvětové\s)(?<!osvětovou\s)\bbesed[aáyěou]\b"
        r"|(?-i:\b(?:ČB|ČOB)\b)", re.I),
    "Orel": re.compile(
        r"\borel\b|\borl[aue]\b|\borlem\b|\borelsk\w+", re.I),
    "DTJ": re.compile(
        r"\bDTJ\b|\bD\.\s?T\.\s?J\b|\bdělnick\w+\s+tělo(?:cvičn|výchovn)\w+\s+jednot\w+", re.I),
    "Divadelní spolek": re.compile(
        r"(?-i:\b(?:SDO|OS|OJ|DJ|JDO|KrDO|ČOS|ČOJ|ČOB)\b)"
        r"|\b(?:spol\w*|sdružení|jednot\w*|kroužk?\w*)\s+divadelních\s+ochotník\w*"
        r"|\bochotnick\w*\s+(?:spol\w*|jednot\w*|družstv\w*|sdružení|klub\w*|besed\w*)"
        r"|\bdivadeln\w*\s+(?:spol(?!ečnost)\w*|jednot\w*|družstv\w*|sdružení)"
        r"|\bdramatick\w*\s+(?:spol(?!ečnost)\w*|klub\w*|jednot\w*)", re.I),
    "Čtenářský spolek": re.compile(r"\bčtenářsk\w*|(?-i:\b(?:ČOS|ČOJ|ČOB)\b)", re.I),
    "Pěvecký spolek": re.compile(r"\bpěveck\w*|\bzpěváck\w*", re.I),
    "Vzdělávací spolek": re.compile(r"\bvzdělávac\w*", re.I),
    "Omladina": re.compile(r"\bomladin\w*", re.I),
    # `\b` after the word, so the lookahead cannot be passed by backtracking into it
    "Dělnický spolek": re.compile(r"\bdělnick\w*\b(?!\s+tělo(?:cvičn|výchovn))", re.I),
    "Katolický spolek": re.compile(r"\bkatolick\w*|\btovaryš\w*", re.I),
    "Národní jednota": re.compile(
        r"(?-i:\bNJ[SPV]?\b)|\bnárodní\w*\s+jednot\w*|\bÚMŠ\b|\bmatic\w*\s+školsk\w*", re.I),
    "Škola": re.compile(
        r"\bstudent\w*|\bstuduj\w*|\bgymn[aá][sz]i\w*|\breálk\w*|\bškol\w*|\bžác\w*|\bžák\w*"
        r"|\bučitel\w*|\bpreparand\w*", re.I),
    "Církev": re.compile(
        r"\bjezuit\w*|\bpiarist\w*|\bpremonstr\w*|\bbenediktin\w*|\bminorit\w*|\bkapucín\w*"
        r"|\bklášter\w*|\bkostel\w*|\bfar[aáuyeěo]\b|\bfarní\w*|\bfarář\w*|\bkaplan\w*", re.I),
}


# abbreviations the key reads two ways: labelled by their first reading, and flagged
AMBIGUOUS_ABBREVIATIONS = {
    "ČOS": "čtenářsko ochotnický spolek, or Česká / Československá obec sokolská",
}
_AMBIGUOUS = re.compile(r"\b(" + "|".join(AMBIGUOUS_ABBREVIATIONS) + r")\b")
# membership of the national union of amateur theatres — a union, not a local host
_UMDOC = re.compile(r"\bÚMDOČ\b|(?i:\bústřední\w*\s+matic\w*\s+divadelního)")


def classify_association(name) -> list[str]:
    """Labels of :data:`ASSOCIATION_PATTERNS` a name or a chronicle line matches (possibly none)."""
    if not isinstance(name, str):
        return []
    return [label for label, pattern in ASSOCIATION_PATTERNS.items() if pattern.search(name)]


def association_counts(ensembles: pd.DataFrame, cutoff: int = PRE_WAR_CUTOFF) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series]:
    """Counts of pre-``cutoff`` ensembles by association, and the unclassified names.

    Returns:
        ``(counts, unclassified)`` — counts has one row per label plus *unclassified*,
        *more than one label* and *all pre-1914 ensembles*; ``unclassified`` is the
        frequency table of the names nothing matched, so the remainder can be read.
    """
    E = ensembles.drop_duplicates("ensemble_id").copy()
    E = E[[starts_before(y, p, cutoff) == "yes" for y, p in zip(E["year_from"], E["year_from_precision"])]]
    labels = E["name"].map(classify_association)
    rows = [(label, int(labels.map(lambda found, lab=label: lab in found).sum()))
            for label in ASSOCIATION_PATTERNS]
    rows += [("unclassified", int((labels.str.len() == 0).sum())),
             ("more than one label", int((labels.str.len() > 1).sum())),
             (f"all ensembles starting before {cutoff}", len(E))]
    counts = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["association", "ensembles"])
    counts["share"] = (counts["ensembles"] / max(len(E), 1)).round(3)
    return counts, E.loc[labels.str.len() == 0, "name"].value_counts()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The chronicle — one note per line, most of them opening with a date
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Every date is read as an *interval* for when the activity started, [start_lo, start_hi],
# and one for when it ended, [end_lo, end_hi]; an unknown bound is NaN.  `1895` is
# [1895, 1895]; `189x` [1890, 1899]; `koncem 19. stol.` [1880, 1899]; `před 1900`
# [NaN, 1899]; `po 1900` [1900, NaN].  :func:`attests_before` reads all of them with
# one rule, so no form is folded into another.
CIRCA_YEARS = 5     # `kolem 1850` is read as 1845–1855: a judgement call (D-137)

_Y = r"(?:1\d\d\d|20[0-2]\d|1\d\d[xX]|20[0-2][xX]|1\d[xX]{2})(?!\d)"
_MONTHS = r"(?:ledna|února|března|dubna|května|června|července|srpna|září|října|listopadu|prosince)"
_DAY_MONTH = rf"(?:\d{{1,2}}\.\s*(?:\d{{1,2}}\.|{_MONTHS})\s*)?"
_DASH = r"\s*[-–—]\s*"

# The part of a century or a decade a phrase names, as (first, last) offsets into it.
_CENTURY_PART = {"whole": (0, 99), "early": (0, 19), "mid": (40, 59), "late": (80, 99),
                 "first_half": (0, 49), "second_half": (50, 99), "turn": (90, 109)}
_DECADE_PART = {"whole": (0, 9), "early": (0, 3), "mid": (3, 6), "late": (7, 9),
                "first_half": (0, 4), "second_half": (5, 9), "turn": (7, 12)}
# (modifier, part, direction) — longest first, so `od konce` is not read as `od`
_MODIFIERS = [
    (r"na\s+přelomu|přelom", "turn", "in"),
    (r"od\s+konce", "late", "from"),
    (r"od\s+(?:počátku|začátku|zač\.|poč\.)", "early", "from"),
    (r"od\s+(?:1\.|první)\s*pol(?:\.|oviny)", "first_half", "from"),
    (r"od\s+(?:poloviny|pol\.)", "mid", "from"),
    (r"od\s+2\.\s*pol(?:\.|oviny)", "second_half", "from"),
    (r"do\s+konce", "late", "until"),
    (r"do\s+(?:poloviny|pol\.)", "mid", "until"),
    (r"koncem|na\s+konci|ke\s+konci|konec", "late", "in"),
    (r"začátkem|počátkem|na\s+(?:začátku|počátku|zač\.|poč\.)|zač\.|poč\.|začátek|počátek",
     "early", "in"),
    (r"(?:ve?\s+)?(?:1\.|první)\s*pol(?:\.|ovin\w*)", "first_half", "in"),
    (r"(?:ve?\s+)?(?:2\.|druh\w+)\s*pol(?:\.|ovin\w*)", "second_half", "in"),
    (r"v\s+polovině|v\s+pol\.|polovinou|kolem\s+poloviny|v\s+půli", "mid", "in"),
    (r"od", "whole", "from"),
    (r"do", "whole", "until"),
    (r"v\s+průběhu|v\s+období|v\s+době|během|ve|v|za", "whole", "in"),
]
_MODIFIER = "|".join(f"(?:{pattern})" for pattern, _, _ in _MODIFIERS)
# several units — `20., 30. a 40. letech`, `od 50. do 80. let`, `koncem 18. a počátkem 19.
# stol.`; a later unit may carry its own modifier, and the end is read as the whole of it
_JOIN = rf"\s*(?:,|a|do\s+konce|do|-|–|až|/)\s*(?:(?:{_MODIFIER}|patrně\s+i)\s*)?"
_PERIOD = re.compile(
    rf"^(?:(?P<mod>{_MODIFIER})\s*)?(?:"
    rf"(?P<d1>\d0)\.?(?:{_JOIN}(?P<d2>\d0)\.?)*\s*(?:léta|let|letech|létech)\b"
    r"(?:\s*(?P<dc>\d{1,2})\.\s*(?:stol\.|století|stol\b|st\.))?"
    rf"|(?P<c1>\d{{1,2}})\.(?:{_JOIN}(?P<c2>\d{{1,2}})\.)*\s*(?:stol\.|století|stol\b|st\.))",
    re.I)

_WAR1 = r"(?:1\.|první|I\.)\s*(?:svět\.|sv\.|světov\w*)\s*(?:v\s*\.|vál[kc]\w*)"
_WAR2 = r"(?:2\.|druh\w*|II\.)\s*(?:svět\.|sv\.|světov\w*)\s*(?:v\s*\.|vál[kc]\w*)"
_ERAS = [   # (pattern, start interval, end interval)
    (rf"před\s+{_WAR1}", (np.nan, 1913), None),
    (rf"(?:za|během|v\s+době|v\s+průběhu|v\s+letech)\s+{_WAR1}", (1914, 1918), None),
    (rf"po\s+{_WAR1}", (1918, np.nan), None),
    (r"(?:za|od)\s+(?:1\.|první)\s+republiky", (1918, 1938), None),
    (rf"před\s+{_WAR2}", (np.nan, 1938), None),
    (rf"(?:za|během|v\s+době|v\s+průběhu|v\s+letech)\s+{_WAR2}"
     r"|(?:za|během|v\s+době)\s+(?:okupace|protektorátu)", (1939, 1945), None),
    (rf"po\s+{_WAR2}|po\s+osvobození", (1945, np.nan), None),
]
_ERA_PATTERNS = [(re.compile(rf"^(?:{p})", re.I), start, end) for p, start, end in _ERAS]

# word + year: (pattern, form)
_WORD_YEAR = re.compile(
    r"^(?:(?:patrně|snad|zřejmě|údajně|prý|asi)\s+(?=od|do|před|po|kolem|v\s))?"
    r"(?P<word>koncem|začátkem|počátkem|od\s+roku|od\s+r\.|od|do\s+roku|do\s+r\.|do|před\s+rokem|před|po\s+roce|po\s+r\.|po"
    r"|kolem\s+roku|kolem|kol\.|okolo|asi\s+v\s+roce|asi|cca\.?|přibližně|snad"
    r"|v\s+letech|mezi\s+lety|v\s+roce|v\s+r\.|roku|r\.|již\s+v\s+roce|již|už)\s+"
    rf"{_DAY_MONTH}(?P<y1>{_Y})(?:(?:{_DASH}|\s+(?:do|až|a)\s+){_DAY_MONTH}(?P<y2>{_Y}))?",
    re.I)
_WORD_FORM = [(r"od\b", "from"), (r"do\b", "until"), (r"před\b", "before"), (r"po\b", "after"),
              (r"kol\b|kolem|okolo|asi|cca|přibližně|snad", "circa"),
              (r"v\s+letech|mezi", "range")]

_RANGE = re.compile(rf"^(?i:dne\s+)?{_DAY_MONTH}(?P<y1>{_Y})(?:{_DASH}{_DAY_MONTH}(?P<y2>{_Y})"
                    r"|-(?P<yy>\d\d)(?![\d.]))")
_SEASON = re.compile(rf"^(?P<y1>{_Y})/(?P<y2>\d{{4}}|\d\d)(?!\d)")
_LIST = re.compile(rf"^(?P<y1>{_Y})(?:(?:\s*,\s*|\s+a\s+|\s+i\s+){_Y})+")
_SINGLE = re.compile(rf"^(?i:dne\s+)?{_DAY_MONTH}(?P<y1>{_Y})")
_ABBREVIATION_FIRST = re.compile(r"^[A-ZÁČĎÉĚÍŇÓŘŠŤÚŮÝŽ]{2,5}\s+(?=\d{4})")

_NO_DATE = {"date_form": None, "date_raw": None, "start_lo": np.nan, "start_hi": np.nan,
            "end_lo": np.nan, "end_hi": np.nan, "century_inferred": False}


def year_span(token: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """``1873`` → (1873, 1873); ``187x`` → (1870, 1879); ``18xx`` → (1800, 1899)."""
    tok = token.strip()
    if tok[-2:].lower() == "xx":
        return int(tok[:2]) * 100, int(tok[:2]) * 100 + 99
    if tok[-1].lower() == "x":
        return int(tok[:3]) * 10, int(tok[:3]) * 10 + 9
    return int(tok), int(tok)


def infer_century(decade: int, context_year) -> int | None:
    """The century of a bare ``80. léta``, from the line above it.

    The chronicle runs forward in time, so the decade is put in the earliest century that
    does not end it before the last dated line: after a 1977 line, ``V 80. letech`` is the
    1980s.  With nothing dated above it there is no reading, and None is returned.
    """
    if context_year is None or pd.isna(context_year):
        return None
    for century in range(1500, 2100, 100):
        if century + decade + 9 >= int(context_year):
            return century
    return None


def _date(form, raw, start=(np.nan, np.nan), end=(np.nan, np.nan), inferred=False) -> dict:
    return {"date_form": form, "date_raw": raw, "start_lo": start[0], "start_hi": start[1],
            "end_lo": end[0], "end_hi": end[1], "century_inferred": inferred}


def _modifier(text: str | None) -> tuple[str, str]:
    if not text:
        return "whole", "in"
    for pattern, part, direction in _MODIFIERS:
        if re.fullmatch(pattern, text.strip(), re.I):
            return part, direction
    return "whole", "in"


def _period(m: re.Match, context_year) -> dict:
    """A century or decade phrase (``koncem 80. let 19. stol.``) as start/end intervals."""
    part, direction = _modifier(m.group("mod"))
    inferred = False
    if m.group("c1"):
        bases = [(int(m.group(g)) - 1) * 100 for g in ("c1", "c2") if m.group(g)]
        offsets = _CENTURY_PART[part]
    else:
        decades = [int(m.group(g)) for g in ("d1", "d2") if m.group(g)]
        if m.group("dc"):
            century = (int(m.group("dc")) - 1) * 100
        else:
            century, inferred = infer_century(decades[0], context_year), True
            if century is None:
                return _date("period, no century", m.group(0))
        bases = [century + d for d in decades]
        offsets = _DECADE_PART[part]
    if part == "turn":                     # `19./20. stol.` names one turn, not two units
        bases = bases[:1]
    first = (bases[0] + offsets[0], bases[0] + offsets[1])
    whole = _DECADE_PART["whole"] if m.group("d1") else _CENTURY_PART["whole"]
    last = (bases[-1] + whole[0], bases[-1] + whole[1]) if len(bases) > 1 else None
    if direction == "until":
        return _date("period", m.group(0), end=last or first, inferred=inferred)
    return _date("period", m.group(0), start=first, end=last or (np.nan, np.nan),
                 inferred=inferred)


def _word_year(m: re.Match) -> dict:
    word = m.group("word").lower()
    form = next((f for p, f in _WORD_FORM if re.match(p, word)), "year")
    y1 = year_span(m.group("y1"))
    y2 = year_span(m.group("y2")) if m.group("y2") else (np.nan, np.nan)
    raw = m.group(0)
    if form == "until":
        return _date("until", raw, end=y1)
    if form == "before":
        return _date("before", raw, start=(np.nan, y1[0] - 1))
    if form == "after":
        return _date("after", raw, start=(y1[0], np.nan))
    if form == "circa":
        return _date("circa", raw, start=(y1[0] - CIRCA_YEARS, y1[1] + CIRCA_YEARS))
    if form == "year" and m.group("y2"):
        form = "range"
    return _date(form, raw, start=y1, end=y2)


def _numeric(line: str) -> dict | None:
    """A line opening with a year: a range, a season, a list or a single year."""
    if (m := _RANGE.match(line)):
        start = year_span(m.group("y1"))
        if m.group("yy"):
            year = start[0] // 100 * 100 + int(m.group("yy"))
            end = (year + 100, year + 100) if year < start[0] else (year, year)
        else:
            end = year_span(m.group("y2"))
        if end[1] < start[0]:              # a later year cannot close an earlier one
            return _date("year", m.group("y1"), start=start)
        return _date("range", m.group(0), start=start, end=end)
    if (m := _SEASON.match(line)):
        start = year_span(m.group("y1"))
        tail = m.group("y2")
        year = int(tail) if len(tail) == 4 else start[0] // 100 * 100 + int(tail)
        return _date("season", m.group(0), start=start, end=(year, year))
    if (m := _LIST.match(line)):
        years = re.findall(_Y, m.group(0))
        return _date("list", m.group(0), start=year_span(years[0]), end=year_span(years[-1]))
    if (m := _SINGLE.match(line)):
        token = m.group("y1")
        form = "century" if token[-2:].lower() == "xx" else "decade" if token[-1] in "xX" else "year"
        return _date(form, m.group(0), start=year_span(token))
    return None


def parse_leading_date(line: str, context_year=None) -> dict:
    """The date a chronicle line opens with, as start/end intervals and a ``date_form``.

    Only the **leading** date is read — a later year inside the line (``1934 22
    představení, 1935 19``) is the line's content, not its date.  Forms: ``year`` /
    ``decade`` / ``century`` (one printed year), ``range``, ``season`` (``1911/12``),
    ``list`` (``1887 a 1912``), ``from``, ``until``, ``before``, ``after``, ``circa``,
    ``period`` (a century or decade phrase), ``era`` (the wars, the First Republic).
    ``context_year`` is the last dated line above, used only to give a bare ``80. léta``
    its century (``century_inferred``).  No date: every field empty, ``date_form`` None.
    """
    text = (line or "").strip()
    for pattern, start, end in _ERA_PATTERNS:
        if (m := pattern.match(text)):
            return _date("era", m.group(0), start=start, end=end or (np.nan, np.nan))
    if (m := _PERIOD.match(text)):
        return _period(m, context_year)
    if (m := _WORD_YEAR.match(text)):
        return _word_year(m)
    if (date := _numeric(text)):
        return date
    # an ensemble's abbreviation before its years: `ŠS 1932 - 1938`, `LS 1928-1929`
    if (m := _ABBREVIATION_FIRST.match(text)) and (date := _numeric(text[m.end():])):
        return date
    return dict(_NO_DATE)


def _is_known(value) -> bool:
    return value is not None and not pd.isna(value)


def attests_before(start_lo, start_hi, end_lo, end_hi, cutoff: int = PRE_WAR_CUTOFF) -> str:
    """Does a dated line put theatre activity before ``cutoff``?  ``yes / no / ambiguous / unknown``.

    With a start: *yes* if it certainly began before the cutoff, *no* if certainly not.
    With only an end (``do 1910``): the activity was going on before that end, so *yes*
    if the end is before the cutoff — otherwise *ambiguous*, never *no*.
    """
    if _is_known(start_lo) or _is_known(start_hi):
        lo = start_lo if _is_known(start_lo) else -np.inf
        hi = start_hi if _is_known(start_hi) else np.inf
        return "yes" if hi < cutoff else "no" if lo >= cutoff else "ambiguous"
    if _is_known(end_hi):
        return "yes" if end_hi < cutoff else "ambiguous"
    return "unknown"


_SEPARATOR = re.compile(r"^[\s\-–—_=*.xX]+$")
_HEADING_START = re.compile(r"^(?:loutkov\w*\s+divadl\w*|historie|zahraniční\s+reprezentace)", re.I)
_CITATION = re.compile(r"^[A-ZÁČĎÉĚÍŇÓŘŠŤÚŮÝŽ][^\d]{1,60}?\s\d{1,2}\.\s*\d{1,2}\.\s*(?P<y>1\d\d\d|20[0-2]\d)"
                       r"\.?(?:,\s*(?:s|č|str)\.\s*[\d\-–]+\.?)?$")
# the okres must be named (a capital), so `okresní přehlídka` is not an admin note
_ADMIN = re.compile(r"^(?i:od|do)\b.{0,40}?\b(?i:okres\w*|okr\.)\s+[A-ZÁČĎÉĚÍŇÓŘŠŤÚŮÝŽ]"
                    r"|(?i:\bsoučástí\s+okresu\b|\bpatřil\w*\s+do\s+okresu\b)")
# LD loutkové divadlo, LS loutkářský soubor / loutková scéna, Lkr loutkářský kroužek,
# DLS dětský loutkářský soubor — the database's key
_PUPPET = re.compile(r"(?i:\bloutk\w*|\bmaňásk\w*)|\b(?:LD|LS|Lkr|DLS)\b")


def chronicle_line_kind(line: str) -> str | None:
    """``separator`` / ``heading`` / ``citation`` / ``admin``, or None for a note.

    A *citation* is a periodical and a full date and nothing else (``Moravský deník
    13.9.1935.``) — the source of the line above, dated by publication.  *Admin* is the
    database's own note on which okres the place belongs to now (``Od 1. 1. 2007 okres
    Praha-východ``), which opens with a date but is no event.
    """
    text = line.strip()
    if _SEPARATOR.match(text):
        return "separator"
    if not re.search(r"\d", text) and len(text) <= 45 and (
            text.endswith(":") or text.isupper() or _HEADING_START.match(text)):
        return "heading"
    if _CITATION.match(text):
        return "citation"
    if len(text) < 120 and _ADMIN.search(text):
        return "admin"
    return None


CHRONICLE_COLUMNS = ["geo_id", "line_no", "kind", "section", "date_form", "date_raw",
                     "start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi", "century_inferred",
                     "associations", "ambiguous_abbreviations", "umdoc", "puppet", "text"]


def _anchor_year(date: dict):
    for key in ("start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi"):
        if not pd.isna(date[key]):
            return date[key]
    return None


def read_chronicle(geo_id: int, text: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Every non-blank line of one place's chronicle, classified and dated.

    ``kind`` is ``event`` (a note with a leading date), ``undated`` (a note without one —
    often a continuation of the line above), or one of :func:`chronicle_line_kind`'s.  A
    heading opens a ``section`` (``puppet`` for *Loutkové divadlo*), which holds until the
    next heading.  ``associations`` are the :data:`ASSOCIATION_PATTERNS` labels the line
    names, ``|``-joined, and ``ambiguous_abbreviations`` any of them that rest on an
    abbreviation the key reads two ways (``ČOS``); ``umdoc`` marks a line naming the
    national union of amateur theatres; ``puppet`` marks puppet theatre, by section or by
    the line's words.
    """
    rows, section, context = [], "main", None
    for line_no, raw in enumerate(text.splitlines()):
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        kind = chronicle_line_kind(line)
        date = dict(_NO_DATE) if kind in ("separator", "heading") else parse_leading_date(line, context)
        if kind in ("heading", "separator"):    # a new block starts its own chronology
            context = None
        if kind == "heading":
            section = "puppet" if _PUPPET.search(line) else line.rstrip(":").strip().casefold()
        if kind is None:
            kind = "event" if _anchor_year(date) is not None else "undated"
        if kind == "event":
            context = _anchor_year(date)
        if kind == "citation":
            year = int(_CITATION.match(line).group("y"))
            date = _date("publication", line, start=(year, year))
        notes = kind in ("event", "undated")
        rows.append({"geo_id": geo_id, "line_no": line_no, "kind": kind, "section": section,
                     **date,
                     "associations": "|".join(classify_association(line)) if notes else "",
                     "ambiguous_abbreviations":
                         "|".join(dict.fromkeys(_AMBIGUOUS.findall(line))) if notes else "",
                     "umdoc": notes and bool(_UMDOC.search(line)),
                     "puppet": notes and (section == "puppet" or bool(_PUPPET.search(line))),
                     "text": line})
    return rows


def chronicle_lines(places: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The chronicle of every place as one table — key ``(geo_id, line_no)``, asserted.

    ``line_no`` is the line's position in the place's ``chronicle_text`` (0-based, blank
    lines counted), so any row leads back to its text.  The events are the rows with
    ``kind == "event"`` (:func:`chronicle_events`).  The text is the database's own and,
    like ``places.csv``, never leaves ``data/``.
    """
    rows = []
    for geo_id, text in zip(places["geo_id"], places["chronicle_text"]):
        if isinstance(text, str):
            rows.extend(read_chronicle(int(geo_id), text))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=CHRONICLE_COLUMNS)
    assert not out.duplicated(["geo_id", "line_no"]).any(), "chronicle: key not unique"
    out["before_1914"] = [attests_before(*r) for r in
                          out[["start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi"]].itertuples(index=False)]
    out.loc[out["kind"] != "event", "before_1914"] = "unknown"
    return out


def chronicle_events(lines: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The dated notes of :func:`chronicle_lines` — the event table."""
    return lines[lines["kind"] == "event"].reset_index(drop=True)


def chronicle_place_summary(places: pd.DataFrame, lines: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per place: how many chronicle events, how many before 1914, which associations.

    One row per place of ``places`` (key ``geo_id``, asserted).  ``earliest_pre_year`` is
    the lowest known bound of the pre-1914 events; ``associations_pre`` the labels any of
    them names, and ``ambiguous_abbreviation_pre`` says whether any of those rests on an
    abbreviation read two ways, so the labels can be re-read without it.  ``umdoc_pre``:
    a pre-1914 event names the national union of amateur theatres (ÚMDOČ).  Puppet
    theatre is counted apart (``n_pre_puppet``) and left out of the rest, since it is a
    different activity, often of children.
    """
    events = chronicle_events(lines)
    pre = events[(events["before_1914"] == "yes") & ~events["puppet"]]
    bound = pre[["start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi"]].min(axis=1)
    per_place = pd.DataFrame({
        "n_events": events.groupby("geo_id").size(),
        "n_pre": pre.groupby("geo_id").size(),
        "n_ambiguous": events[events["before_1914"] == "ambiguous"].groupby("geo_id").size(),
        "n_pre_puppet": events[(events["before_1914"] == "yes") & events["puppet"]]
        .groupby("geo_id").size(),
        "earliest_pre_year": bound.groupby(pre["geo_id"]).min(),
        "associations_pre": pre.groupby("geo_id")["associations"].agg(
            lambda s: "|".join(sorted({a for v in s for a in v.split("|") if a}))),
        "ambiguous_abbreviation_pre": pre.groupby("geo_id")["ambiguous_abbreviations"].agg(
            lambda s: bool((s != "").any())),
        "umdoc_pre": pre.groupby("geo_id")["umdoc"].any(),
    })
    out = places[["geo_id"]].merge(per_place, left_on="geo_id", right_index=True,
                                   how="left", validate="1:1")
    counts = ["n_events", "n_pre", "n_ambiguous", "n_pre_puppet"]
    out[counts] = out[counts].fillna(0).astype(int)
    out["associations_pre"] = out["associations_pre"].fillna("")
    flags = ["ambiguous_abbreviation_pre", "umdoc_pre"]
    out[flags] = out[flags].astype("boolean").fillna(False).astype(bool)
    assert len(out) == len(places) and out["geo_id"].is_unique
    return out


def century_inference_check(lines: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    """How often :func:`infer_century` would have been right where the century is printed.

    Takes every decade phrase that names its century (``V 80. letech 19. stol.``), drops
    the century, infers it from the dated line above as a bare one would be, and compares.
    """
    pattern = re.compile(r"(?P<d>\d0)\.?.*?(?:léta|let|letech|létech)\b\s*(?P<c>\d{1,2})\.", re.I)
    # the parser's context: the dated line above, inside the same block (headings and
    # separators start a new one)
    block = lines["kind"].isin(["heading", "separator"]).groupby(lines["geo_id"]).cumsum()
    events = lines.assign(block=block)[lines["kind"] == "event"].copy()
    events["anchor"] = events[["start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi"]].bfill(axis=1).iloc[:, 0]
    events["previous"] = events.groupby(["geo_id", "block"])["anchor"].shift()
    checked = right = 0
    for raw, inferred, previous in zip(events["date_raw"], events["century_inferred"],
                                       events["previous"]):
        m = pattern.search(raw or "") if not inferred else None
        if m is None or pd.isna(previous):
            continue
        checked += 1
        right += infer_century(int(m.group("d")), previous) == (int(m.group("c")) - 1) * 100
    return {"checked": checked, "right": right, "share_right": round(right / max(checked, 1), 3)}


def chronicle_report(places: pd.DataFrame, lines: pd.DataFrame, ensembles: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    """Print what the chronicle parser found: kinds, date forms, the pre-1914 yield."""
    events = chronicle_events(lines)
    summary = chronicle_place_summary(places, lines)
    dates = place_dates(places, ensembles)
    print("\n── chronicle lines by kind\n" + lines["kind"].value_counts().to_string())
    print("\n── events by date form\n" + events["date_form"].value_counts().to_string())
    print(f"\n── century of a bare decade inferred on {int(events['century_inferred'].sum()):,} events;"
          f" check where it is printed: {century_inference_check(lines)}")
    print("\n── events: activity before 1914?\n" + events["before_1914"].value_counts().to_string())
    has_pre = summary.set_index("geo_id")["n_pre"] > 0
    no_ensemble = ~dates.set_index("geo_id")["ensemble_pre"]
    print(f"\nplaces with a pre-1914 (non-puppet) chronicle event: {int(has_pre.sum()):,}"
          f" — of them with no ensemble certainly before 1914: {int((has_pre & no_ensemble).sum()):,}")
    pre = events[(events["before_1914"] == "yes") & ~events["puppet"]]
    labels = pre["associations"].str.split("|").explode()
    print("\n── pre-1914 events by association named (an event can name several)\n"
          + labels[labels != ""].value_counts().to_string()
          + f"\nnaming none: {int((pre['associations'] == '').sum()):,} of {len(pre):,}")
    print(f"pre-1914 events resting on an abbreviation read two ways (ČOS):"
          f" {int((pre['ambiguous_abbreviations'] != '').sum()):,};"
          f" naming ÚMDOČ: {int(pre['umdoc'].sum()):,}"
          f" (places: {int(summary['umdoc_pre'].sum()):,})")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Clauses — one line is often several events (0.4.0)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# `1887-1934 SDO, 1914 32 členů.` is a company's span and a membership count a year
# apart; `1908 DS Sokol Na prahu života, 1930 Teta Fany` two performances 22 years apart.
# A line is cut wherever a new *date* opens after a comma, a semicolon or a full stop —
# and only there, so a clause always starts with its date or is the line's first.  Never
# cut: inside brackets or a quoted title; inside the line's own leading date (`1887, 1888
# a 1890 hráli`); a *report* — a line opening with a full day-and-month date or with
# `YEAR -`, or ending in a periodical citation — which is one dated newspaper extract and
# whose later dates (`bude opakována 23.2.1913`) are its content.  A trailing citation is
# set aside (`citation`), never read as the event's date (D-140).
_CLAUSE_BOUNDARY = re.compile(r"(?:[,;]|\.(?=\s))\s+")
# a word that may stand before the new clause's date: `…her. Poté do 1937 56 her.`
_CLAUSE_LEAD = re.compile(r"^(?:poté|pak|potom|později|znovu|opět|též|také|ale|však|dále"
                          r"|naposled|naposledy|zejména|hlavně)\s+", re.I)


def _after_lead(piece: str) -> str:
    return piece[m.end():] if (m := _CLAUSE_LEAD.match(piece)) else piece
# words a full stop ends without ending the sentence — `zal. 1895`, `r. 1890`, `19. stol.`
_ABBREVIATION_WORDS = {
    "r", "zal", "stol", "st", "sv", "svět", "č", "s", "str", "kol", "cca", "tzv", "tj",
    "např", "ad", "uč", "řed", "p", "pp", "ev", "hl", "div", "spol", "ochot", "odb", "nar",
    "zem", "obnov", "přejm", "zah", "zan", "ust", "pol", "zač", "poč", "resp", "aj", "atd", "mj", "srv", "viz",
    "inf", "ing", "mudr", "judr", "phdr", "dr", "prof", "mgr", "fr", "jos", "ant", "jan"}
_QUOTED = re.compile(r'"[^"]*"|“[^”“]*[”“]|„[^“”]*[“”]|»[^«]*«|«[^»]*»')
_TRAILING_CITATION = re.compile(
    r"(?:\s*\((?:Informac\w*|Inf\.)[^)]*\)\.?"
    r"|\s*Inf\.\s*ex:.*"
    r"|\s+[A-ZÁČĎÉĚÍŇÓŘŠŤÚŮÝŽ][\w.]*(?:\s+[\w.]+){0,5}\s+\d{1,2}\.\s*\d{1,2}\.\s*1\d\d\d\.?)\s*$")
_FULL_DATE_LEAD = re.compile(rf"^(?i:dne\s+)?\d{{1,2}}\.\s*(?:\d{{1,2}}\.|{_MONTHS})\s*1\d\d\d")
_DASH_LEAD = re.compile(rf"^(?:{_Y}|{_DAY_MONTH}{_Y})\s*[-–—]\s*(?=[^\d\s])")
_YEAR_TOKEN = re.compile(rf"(?<![\d.]){_Y}")

CLAUSE_COLUMNS = ["geo_id", "line_no", "clause_no", "line_kind", "section", "report",
                  "date_source", "date_form", "date_raw", "start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo",
                  "end_hi", "century_inferred", "years_listed", "years_inside", "date_only",
                  "associations", "ambiguous_abbreviations", "puppet", "cues", "citation", "text"]


def _protected_spans(text: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Character spans a clause boundary may not fall in: brackets (nested) and quotes."""
    spans, depth, opened = [], 0, 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(text):
        if ch == "(":
            if depth == 0:
                opened = i
            depth += 1
        elif ch == ")" and depth:
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                spans.append((opened, i + 1))
    if depth:                                   # an unclosed bracket runs to the end
        spans.append((opened, len(text)))
    spans += [m.span() for m in _QUOTED.finditer(text)]
    return spans


def is_report(line: str) -> bool:
    """A dated newspaper extract, read as one event: never cut into clauses."""
    text = (line or "").strip()
    return bool(_FULL_DATE_LEAD.match(text) or _DASH_LEAD.match(text)
                or _TRAILING_CITATION.search(text))


def _ends_abbreviation(text: str, stop: int) -> bool:
    """Does the full stop at ``stop`` close an abbreviation or an ordinal rather than a sentence?"""
    word = re.search(r"(\w+)$", text[:stop])
    if word is None:
        return False
    token = word.group(1)
    return (token.casefold() in _ABBREVIATION_WORDS or len(token) == 1
            or (token.isdigit() and len(token) <= 2))


def clause_cuts(line: str, context_year=None) -> list[int]:
    """Character offsets at which a line is cut into clauses (the first, 0, included)."""
    text = line or ""
    cuts = [0]
    if is_report(text):
        return cuts
    lead = parse_leading_date(text.strip(), context_year)
    lead_end = text.find(lead["date_raw"]) + len(lead["date_raw"]) if lead["date_raw"] else 0
    spans = _protected_spans(text)
    for m in _CLAUSE_BOUNDARY.finditer(text):
        at = m.end()
        if at <= lead_end or any(a <= m.start() < b for a, b in spans):
            continue
        if text[m.start()] == "." and _ends_abbreviation(text, m.start()):
            continue
        if parse_leading_date(_after_lead(text[at:]), context_year)["date_form"] is not None:
            cuts.append(at)
    return cuts


def split_clauses(line: str, line_date: dict | None = None, context_year=None) -> list[dict]:
    """One chronicle line as its dated clauses.

    The first clause carries the line's own date (``line_date``, the dict
    :func:`parse_leading_date` returns — ``date_source = "line"``, or ``"none"`` for an
    undated line); every later one starts with its own (``"own"``), and a bare decade in it
    takes its century from the clause before.  ``years_inside`` lists every other year the
    clause prints (``zanikl 1931``, a bracketed `zal. 1895`), ``years_listed`` the years of
    a leading list (``1910 a 1913`` — two years, not a span), ``date_only`` marks a clause
    that is nothing but its date (``…, 1907, 1910`` — the activity of the clause before,
    again).  A trailing periodical citation is moved to ``citation``.
    """
    text = (line or "").strip()
    report, citation = is_report(text), ""
    if (m := _TRAILING_CITATION.search(text)) and m.start() > 0:
        citation, text = m.group(0).strip(), text[:m.start()].rstrip()
    first = dict(line_date) if line_date is not None else parse_leading_date(text, context_year)
    cuts = [0] if report else clause_cuts(text, context_year)
    clauses, context = [], _anchor_year(first) if first["date_form"] else context_year
    for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(cuts, cuts[1:] + [len(text)])):
        piece = re.sub(r"[\s,;]+$", "", text[a:b]).strip()
        if i == 0:
            date, source = first, "line" if _anchor_year(first) is not None else "none"
        else:
            date, source = parse_leading_date(_after_lead(piece), context), "own"
            context = _anchor_year(date) if _anchor_year(date) is not None else context
        raw = date["date_raw"] or ""
        rest = piece[piece.find(raw) + len(raw):] if raw and raw in piece else piece
        listed = _YEAR_TOKEN.findall(raw) if date["date_form"] == "list" else []
        clauses.append({
            "clause_no": i, "date_source": source, **date,
            "years_listed": "|".join(listed),
            "years_inside": "|".join(_YEAR_TOKEN.findall(rest)),
            "date_only": bool(raw) and not re.search(r"\w", rest),
            "citation": citation if i == len(cuts) - 1 else "",
            "text": piece})
    return clauses


def chronicle_clauses(lines: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Every event and undated note of :func:`chronicle_lines` cut into dated clauses.

    Key ``(geo_id, line_no, clause_no)``, asserted; every line yields at least one clause
    and the clauses of a line, joined, give back its text less the trailing citation.  The
    first clause keeps the line's date exactly as :func:`chronicle_lines` read it.
    ``report`` marks a line kept whole (:func:`is_report`).  ``associations`` and
    ``puppet`` are the clause's own (a puppet section makes every clause in it puppet);
    the line's are in ``chronicle_lines``.  ``cues`` are :func:`event_cues`, not codes.
    """
    notes = lines[lines["kind"].isin(["event", "undated"])]
    date_cols = ["date_form", "date_raw", "start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi",
                 "century_inferred"]
    rows = []
    for r in notes.itertuples(index=False):
        line_date = {c: getattr(r, c) for c in date_cols}
        line_date["date_raw"] = line_date["date_raw"] if isinstance(line_date["date_raw"], str) else None
        line_date["date_form"] = line_date["date_form"] if isinstance(line_date["date_form"], str) else None
        context = _anchor_year(line_date) if line_date["date_form"] else None
        report = is_report(r.text)
        for clause in split_clauses(r.text, line_date, context):
            rows.append({
                "geo_id": r.geo_id, "line_no": r.line_no, "line_kind": r.kind,
                "section": r.section, "report": report, **clause,
                "associations": "|".join(classify_association(clause["text"])),
                "ambiguous_abbreviations": "|".join(dict.fromkeys(_AMBIGUOUS.findall(clause["text"]))),
                "puppet": r.section == "puppet" or bool(_PUPPET.search(clause["text"])),
                "cues": "|".join(event_cues(clause["text"], clause["date_raw"]))})
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=CLAUSE_COLUMNS)
    assert not out.duplicated(["geo_id", "line_no", "clause_no"]).any(), "clauses: key not unique"
    assert out[["geo_id", "line_no"]].drop_duplicates().shape[0] == len(notes), "clauses: a line lost"
    out["before_1914"] = [attests_before(*r) for r in
                          out[["start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi"]].itertuples(index=False)]
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Event cues — the codebook's draft, before the author rules on it
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One pattern per codebook type, word-anchored on the stem.  A *cue* is not a code: it says
# the clause uses a word the type is written in, so the codebook page can show how often
# each type would come up and what it would catch.  Types are not exclusive (`1895 zal.
# SDO, hrál v hostinci` is a founding, activity and a venue).  Which of them enter the
# measure, and how, is the author's ruling (codebook page); the model pass reads the
# clauses the cues leave open.
EVENT_CUES: dict[str, re.Pattern] = {
    "founded": re.compile(
        r"\bzal\.|\bzaložen\w*|\bzaložil\w*|\bvznik\w*|\bustaven\w*|\bustavil\w*"
        r"|\butvořil\w*|\bzřízen\w*", re.I),
    "statutes": re.compile(r"\bstanov\w*|\bregistr\w*", re.I),
    "permit": re.compile(r"\bpovol\w*|\blicenc\w*|\bkoncese\w*", re.I),
    "active": re.compile(
        r"\bhrál\w*|\bhrálo\b|\bhrával\w*|\bčinn\w*|\bpůsobil\w*|\bpůsobí\b|\bpořádal\w*"
        r"|\bprovozoval\w*|\baktivn\w*|\bzaznamenán\w*|\bdolož\w*", re.I),
    "performance": re.compile(
        r"\bsehrál\w*|\bsehrán\w*|\bsehraj\w*|\buvedl\w*|\buveden\w*|\bprovedl\w*|\bproveden\w*"
        r"|\bpředstavení\b|\bdávali\b|\bdáván\w*|\bveselohr\w*|\bfrašk\w*|\bčinohr\w*|\boperet\w*"
        r"|\bzpěvohr\w*|\bpremiér\w*|\bhru\b|\bhra\b", re.I),
    "title": re.compile(r'"[^"]{2,}"|“[^”“]{2,}[”“]|„[^“”]{2,}[“”]'),
    "count": re.compile(
        r"\b\d+\s*(?:her|hry|představení|premiér\w*|inscenac\w*|činoher|operet|kusů|kusy)\b"
        r"|\b\d{1,2}\s*[x×]\b", re.I),             # `3x`, not the decade `188x`
    "attendance": re.compile(
        r"\bnávštěv\w*|\bdivák\w*|\bobecenstv\w*|\bposluchač\w*|\bvyprodán\w*"
        r"|\bpro\s+\d+\s*(?:osob|lidí|diváků)|\b\d+\s*(?:diváků|osob)\b", re.I),
    "proceeds": re.compile(r"\bve\s+prospěch\b|\bvýtěž\w*|\bvýnos\w*|\bna\s+fond\w*", re.I),
    "national_theatre": re.compile(
        r"\bnárodní\w*\s+divadl\w*|\bdivadla\s+národního\b|\bND\b", re.I),
    "venue": re.compile(
        r"\bhostin\w*|\bhospod\w*|\bsál\w*|\bradnic\w*|\bzám(?:ek|ku|ecké\w*)\b|\bsokolovn\w*"
        r"|\bv\s+přírodě\b|\bletní\s+(?:scén|divadl)\w*|\bjevišt\w*|\bdekorac\w*|\bopon\w*", re.I),
    "building": re.compile(r"\bpostav\w*|\bstavb\w*|\bvyhoř\w*|\bpožár\w*|\bbudov\w*", re.I),
    # played in German, or a German theatre noun — not a place name (`Německý Brod`) nor
    # `německý národnostní tlak` (0.5.0, D-141)
    "german": re.compile(
        r"\bněmecky\b|\bněmčin\w*|\bdeutsch\w*|\bněmeck\w*\s+(?:ochotnick\w*|divadl\w*"
        r"|představení|hr[auy]\b|spol\w*|jednot\w*|OS\b)", re.I),
    "latin": re.compile(r"\blatin\w*|\blatinsk\w*", re.I),
    "first": re.compile(r"\bpoprvé\b|\bprvní\s+(?:představení|hr[auy]|divadel\w*|zpráv\w*|doklad\w*"
                        r"|zmín\w*|česk\w*)", re.I),
    "travelling": re.compile(r"\bkočovn\w*|\bhereck\w+\s+společnost\w*|\bdivadeln\w+\s+společnost\w*"
                             r"|\bspolečnost\w*\s+(?:[A-ZČŘŠŽ]\.\s*)?[A-ZČŘŠŽ]\w+(?:ov[aýy]|ého)\b"),
    "school_church": re.compile(r"\bstudent\w*|\bstudují\w*|\bžác\w*|\bžák\w*|\bškol\w*|\bgymn\w*"
                                r"|\bjezuit\w*|\bpiarist\w*|\bklášter\w*|\bseminar\w*|\bfarář\w*", re.I),
    "ban": re.compile(r"\bzakáz\w*|\bzákaz\w*|\bnepovol\w*|\bzamítn\w*|\bcenzur\w*|\bkonfisk\w*"
                      r"|\brozpušt\w*|\bzastaven\w*", re.I),
    "pause": re.compile(r"\bpřeruš\w*|\bpauz\w*|\bnehrál\w*|\bútlum\w*|\bochabl\w*|\bstagnov\w*"
                        r"|\bnečinn\w*|\bnepracoval\w*", re.I),
    "ended": re.compile(r"\bzanik\w*|\bzánik\w*|\bukončen\w*|\brozešel\b|\brozpadl\w*|\bzrušen\w*"
                        r"|\blikvid\w*|\bskončil\w*", re.I),
    "renamed": re.compile(r"\bpřejmenov\w*|\bnázv\w*|\bnázev\b|\bpřeměnil\w*|\bsloučen\w*"
                          r"|\bsplynul\w*|\bpřevzal\w*|\bpřešel\b", re.I),
    "members": re.compile(r"\b\d+\s*člen\w*|\bčlenem\b|\bčlenové\b|\bÚMDOČ\b"),
    "hedged": re.compile(r"\bpatrně\b|\bsnad\b|\bzřejmě\b|\búdajně\b|\bprý\b|\bmožná\b"
                         r"|\bpravděpodobně\b|\?", re.I),
}


# `1851-1893 Thalia.`, `Od 1885 jako SDO Tyl.` — a date and a company's name and nothing
# else: the chronicle's commonest form, a company listed as active.  Read structurally:
# no other cue, and at most this many words after the date.
LISTED_MAX_WORDS = 8


def event_cues(text, date_raw=None) -> list[str]:
    """The :data:`EVENT_CUES` types a clause's words point to (possibly none).

    With ``date_raw`` (the clause's leading date) a clause that is a date and a short name
    and nothing any cue reads is ``listed`` — a company recorded as active.
    """
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        return []
    found = [label for label, pattern in EVENT_CUES.items() if pattern.search(text)]
    if isinstance(date_raw, str) and date_raw and not set(found) - {"hedged"}:
        rest = text[text.find(date_raw) + len(date_raw):] if date_raw in text else text
        words = re.findall(r"\w+", rest)
        if 0 < len(words) <= LISTED_MAX_WORDS:
            found.append("listed")
    return found


def cue_table(clauses: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Pre-1914 non-puppet clauses by cue type, with the remainder no cue reaches.

    ``hedged`` and ``title`` are attributes, so a clause carrying only them counts as
    having no type.
    """
    pre = clauses[(clauses["before_1914"] == "yes") & ~clauses["puppet"]]
    cues = pd.Series([event_cues(t, d) for t, d in zip(pre["text"], pre["date_raw"])],
                     index=pre.index)
    rows = [(label, int(cues.map(lambda found, lab=label: lab in found).sum()))
            for label in [*EVENT_CUES, "listed"]]
    typed = cues.map(lambda found: bool(set(found) - {"hedged", "title"}))
    rows += [("no type (only an attribute, or nothing)", int((~typed).sum())),
             ("pre-1914 non-puppet clauses", len(pre))]
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["cue", "clauses"])
    out["share"] = (out["clauses"] / max(len(pre), 1)).round(3)
    return out


def clause_report(clauses: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    """Print what the splitter did: lines cut, clauses per line, the pre-1914 yield."""
    per_line = clauses.groupby(["geo_id", "line_no"]).size()
    print("\n── chronicle clauses: lines by number of clauses\n"
          + per_line.value_counts().sort_index().to_string())
    print(f"lines kept whole as reports: {int(clauses.drop_duplicates(['geo_id', 'line_no'])['report'].sum()):,}")
    print("\n── clauses by where their date comes from\n"
          + clauses["date_source"].value_counts().to_string())
    pre = clauses[(clauses["before_1914"] == "yes") & ~clauses["puppet"]]
    lines_pre = clauses[(clauses["clause_no"] == 0) & (clauses["before_1914"] == "yes") & ~clauses["puppet"]]
    print(f"\npre-1914 non-puppet clauses: {len(pre):,} (from the lines' own dates alone: {len(lines_pre):,})"
          f"; in {pre['geo_id'].nunique():,} places")
    undated = clauses[(clauses["date_source"] == "none") & clauses["years_inside"].ne("")]
    early = undated["years_inside"].map(lambda s: any(int(y[:4].replace("x", "0")) < PRE_WAR_CUTOFF
                                                      for y in s.split("|")))
    print(f"undated clauses printing a year inside: {len(undated):,}, a pre-1914 one: {int(early.sum()):,}")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The author's rulings (codebook page, 2026-10-28; D-141) and the rules coder
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Role of each event type in the measure.  "Activity …" puts Czech theatre in the place
# and year; "… column" gives the type a panel column of its own; "Coded only" keeps it in
# the evidence table.  `listed` and `active` are carried by `ensembles_active`, so their
# "column" is that one.
CODEBOOK_ROLES = {
    "listed": "Activity + column", "active": "Activity + column", "founded": "Activity + column",
    "performance": "Activity + column", "title": "Column only", "count": "Activity + column",
    "attendance": "Column only", "proceeds": "Column only", "national_theatre": "Column only",
    "statutes": "Activity + column", "permit": "Activity + column", "first": "Activity + column",
    "german": "Column only", "school_church": "Activity + column", "travelling": "Activity + column",
    "venue": "Coded only", "building": "Coded only", "members": "Coded only", "renamed": "Coded only",
    "ended": "Coded only", "pause": "Coded only", "ban": "Coded only",
    "latin": "Column only",      # added with the narrower German cue (D-141), as German is
}
ACTIVITY_TYPES = {t for t, role in CODEBOOK_ROLES.items() if role.startswith("Activity")}
EVENT_COLUMNS = ["founded", "statutes", "permit", "first", "performance", "proceeds",
                 "national_theatre", "school_church", "travelling", "german", "bilingual",
                 "latin", "attendance"]
# B9: from the national revival to the last year before the war
PANEL_FIRST_YEAR, PANEL_LAST_YEAR = 1780, 1913
# B6: school and church theatre enters the Czech measure from 1848; before, a column only
SCHOOL_CHURCH_FROM = 1848
# company evidence: a clause that records a company existing over time, not one evening
COMPANY_TYPES = {"listed", "active", "founded", "statutes"}
# B2: a chronicle company and an ensemble-list row are one company when their starts are
# this close — on years alone, since a label like SDO names many different companies
MATCH_START_YEARS = 1

_YEAR4 = r"(1[5-9]\d\d)(?!\d)"
# an end the clause prints after its leading date: `činný do 1938`, `zanikl 1931`
_END_INSIDE = re.compile(
    r"(?:\baž\s+do|\bnejméně\s+do|\bdo|\bzanikl\w*|\bukončen\w*\s+(?:v\s+)?(?:r\.\s*|roce\s+)?"
    r"|\bčinn\w*(?:\s+(?:ještě|i|patrně|zřejmě|nejméně))*(?:\s+(?:v\s+)?(?:r\.|roce))?)"
    rf"\s+(?:r\.\s*|roku\s+)?{_YEAR4}", re.I)
# not a date's year (`2.4.1866 hry`), and not `kusů`, which is as often scenery as plays
_COUNT_NUMBER = re.compile(
    r"(?<![\d.])(\d{1,3})\s*(?:her|hry|představení|premiér\w*|inscenac\w*|činoher|operet)\b", re.I)
_ATTENDANCE_NUMBER = re.compile(r"\b(\d{2,5})\s*(?:diváků|osob|posluchačů|lidí)\b", re.I)
_QUOTED_TITLE = re.compile(r'"([^"]{2,80})"|“([^”“]{2,80})[”“]|„([^“”]{2,80})[“”]')
_CZECH_WORD = re.compile(r"\bčesk\w*|\bčesky\b", re.I)


def _title_key(title: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\W+", " ", strip_diacritics(title)).strip().casefold()


def code_clause(text: str, date_raw, types: list[str]) -> dict:
    """What the rules read in one clause beyond its cue types.

    ``end_inside`` is an end year printed after the leading date (``činný do 1938``);
    ``count_stated`` the plays or performances it numbers, summed over every number set
    before a play word (``8 představení a 3 hry`` is 11); ``titles`` the quoted play
    titles, as keys;
    ``attendance_n`` the largest audience it numbers; ``bilingual`` a German clause that
    also names Czech.
    """
    raw = date_raw if isinstance(date_raw, str) else ""
    rest = text[text.find(raw) + len(raw):] if raw and raw in text else text
    end = _END_INSIDE.search(rest)
    counts = [int(n) for n in _COUNT_NUMBER.findall(rest)]
    audience = [int(n) for n in _ATTENDANCE_NUMBER.findall(rest)]
    titles = sorted({_title_key(next(g for g in m.groups() if g)) for m in _QUOTED_TITLE.finditer(text)})
    return {"end_inside": int(end.group(1)) if end else np.nan,
            "count_stated": sum(counts) if counts else np.nan,
            "titles": "|".join(t for t in titles if t),
            "attendance_n": max(audience) if audience else np.nan,
            "bilingual": "german" in types and bool(_CZECH_WORD.search(text))}


def code_clauses(clauses: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """:func:`chronicle_clauses` with the rulings applied (D-141): one row per clause, same key.

    Adds :func:`code_clause`'s fields and
    ``czech_activity`` — the clause puts *Czech* amateur theatre in its place: some type
    has an Activity role (a quoted title is a performance), and it is not German or
    bilingual (B8), not puppet theatre, and not school or church theatre before 1848
    (B6; one that may straddle 1848 counts, and is possible only by its interval);
    ``company`` — it records a company over time (listed, active, founded, statutes);
    ``hedged`` — read as possible only (B4);
    ``needs_model`` — the rules leave it open: an undated clause printing a year inside
    (B11), or a dated one no type reaches.
    """
    out = clauses.copy()
    types = out["cues"].fillna("").str.split("|").map(lambda t: [x for x in t if x])
    coded = pd.DataFrame([code_clause(t, d, ty) for t, d, ty in zip(out["text"], out["date_raw"], types)],
                         index=out.index)
    out = pd.concat([out, coded], axis=1)
    has = lambda name: types.map(lambda t, n=name: n in t)                      # noqa: E731
    activity = types.map(lambda t: bool(ACTIVITY_TYPES & (set(t) | ({"performance"} if "title" in t else set()))))
    early_school = has("school_church") & (out["start_hi"] < SCHOOL_CHURCH_FROM)
    out["czech_activity"] = activity & ~has("german") & ~out["puppet"] & ~early_school
    out["company"] = types.map(lambda t: bool(COMPANY_TYPES & set(t))) & ~out["puppet"] & ~has("german")
    out["performance"] = has("performance") | has("title") | has("count")
    out["hedged"] = has("hedged")
    no_type = types.map(lambda t: not (set(t) - {"hedged", "title"}))
    out["needs_model"] = ((out["date_source"] == "none") & out["years_inside"].fillna("").ne("")) | (
        (out["date_source"] != "none") & no_type)
    for column in ("founded", "statutes", "permit", "first", "proceeds", "national_theatre",
                   "school_church", "travelling", "german", "latin", "attendance", "pause"):
        out[column] = has(column)
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The evidence table — every dated record of theatre in one interval form
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
EVIDENCE_COLUMNS = ["evidence_id", "geo_id", "source", "source_key", "company_id",
                    "start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi", "open_end", "hedged",
                    "czech_activity", "company", "performance", "count_stated", "titles",
                    "attendance_n", "pause", "puppet", *[c for c in EVENT_COLUMNS if c != "performance"]]


def _span_from_precision(year, precision) -> tuple[float, float]:
    if pd.isna(year) or precision not in _SPAN_OF:
        return np.nan, np.nan
    return float(year), float(year) + _SPAN_OF[precision]


def active_decade_list(value) -> list[int]:
    """``ensemble_pages.active_decades`` (``1880|1890``) as first years of decades."""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return [int(x) for x in value.split("|") if x.strip()]
    if value is None or pd.isna(value):
        return []
    return [int(value)]


def _ensemble_company_id(geo_id, ensemble_id) -> str:
    return f"{int(geo_id)}:e{int(ensemble_id)}"


def _with_pages(ensembles: pd.DataFrame, pages: pd.DataFrame | None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The ensemble list with its page's end and decades (blank where there is no page)."""
    E = ensembles.copy()
    columns = ["ended_year", "ended_precision", "active_decades"]
    if pages is None:
        return E.assign(ended_year=np.nan, ended_precision="missing", active_decades=None)
    n = len(E)
    E = E.merge(pages[["ensemble_id", *columns]], on="ensemble_id", how="left", validate="m:1")
    assert len(E) == n, "ensemble pages: the merge changed the list"
    return E


def _ensemble_evidence(ensembles: pd.DataFrame, pages: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The ensemble list as company evidence: one row per ensemble and place, dated start.

    With the ensemble pages (D-145), a list row with no end takes the page's printed end
    (*Ukončení činnosti / poslední zpráva*), so it is certain from start to end; and a page
    that lists decades (*Působení*) closes the open end — the row becomes its start alone —
    and adds one ``ensemble_decade`` row per decade, a point as wide as the decade
    (possible across it, certain in no year, B10), under the ensemble's ``company_id``.
    """
    E = _with_pages(ensembles, pages)
    start = [_span_from_precision(y, p) for y, p in zip(E["year_from"], E["year_from_precision"])]
    end = [_span_from_precision(y, p) for y, p in zip(E["year_to"], E["year_to_precision"])]
    page_end = [_span_from_precision(y, p) for y, p in zip(E["ended_year"], E["ended_precision"])]
    end = [pe if pd.isna(e[0]) else e for e, pe in zip(end, page_end)]
    decades = E["active_decades"].map(active_decade_list).to_numpy()
    out = pd.DataFrame({
        "geo_id": E["geo_id"].astype(int), "source": "ensemble",
        "source_key": E["ensemble_id"].astype(int).astype(str),
        "start_lo": [s[0] for s in start], "start_hi": [s[1] for s in start],
        "end_lo": [e[0] for e in end], "end_hi": [e[1] for e in end]})
    out["open_end"] = out["end_lo"].isna() & np.array([not d for d in decades], dtype=bool)
    out["puppet"] = E["name"].fillna("").str.contains(_PUPPET).to_numpy()
    out["german"] = E["name"].fillna("").map(lambda n: bool(EVENT_CUES["german"].search(n))).to_numpy()
    out["company"] = ~out["puppet"] & ~out["german"]
    out["czech_activity"] = out["company"]
    flags = ["puppet", "german", "company", "czech_activity"]
    rows = [{"geo_id": r.geo_id, "source": "ensemble_decade", "source_key": f"{r.source_key}.{d}",
             "start_lo": float(d), "start_hi": float(d + 9), "end_lo": np.nan, "end_hi": np.nan,
             "open_end": False, **{f: getattr(r, f) for f in flags},
             "company_id": _ensemble_company_id(r.geo_id, r.source_key) if r.company else pd.NA}
            for r, listed in zip(out.itertuples(index=False), decades) for d in listed]
    decade_rows = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=[*out.columns, "company_id"])
    return pd.concat([out[out["start_lo"].notna()], decade_rows], ignore_index=True)


def ensemble_chronicle_clauses(pages: pd.DataFrame, ensembles: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Each ensemble page's own chronicle, read and cut as a place's is (D-145).

    One block per ensemble and place it is listed under (as :func:`_ensemble_evidence`
    has one row per ensemble and place), read by :func:`read_chronicle` and
    :func:`chronicle_clauses`.  Key ``(ensemble_id, geo_id, line_no, clause_no)``,
    asserted.  A puppet ensemble's clauses are all puppet; ``ensemble_german`` marks a
    German ensemble's, whose evidence never counts as Czech.
    """
    columns = ["ensemble_id", *CLAUSE_COLUMNS, "before_1914", "ensemble_german"]
    text = pages.set_index("ensemble_id")["chronicle_text"]
    listed = ensembles[["ensemble_id", "geo_id", "name"]].drop_duplicates(["ensemble_id", "geo_id"])
    parts = []
    for ensemble_id, geo_id, name in listed.itertuples(index=False):
        chronicle = text.get(ensemble_id)
        if not isinstance(chronicle, str):
            continue
        lines = pd.DataFrame(read_chronicle(int(geo_id), chronicle), columns=CHRONICLE_COLUMNS)
        clauses = chronicle_clauses(lines)
        if clauses.empty:
            continue
        name = name if isinstance(name, str) else ""
        clauses.insert(0, "ensemble_id", int(ensemble_id))
        clauses["puppet"] = clauses["puppet"] | bool(_PUPPET.search(name))
        clauses["ensemble_german"] = bool(EVENT_CUES["german"].search(name))
        parts.append(clauses)
    out = pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True) if parts else pd.DataFrame(columns=columns)
    assert not out.duplicated(["ensemble_id", "geo_id", "line_no", "clause_no"]).any(), \
        "ensemble clauses: key not unique"
    return out[columns]


def _clause_evidence(coded: pd.DataFrame, source: str = "chronicle") -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Chronicle clauses the rulings give a role, in interval form.

    A clause with no printed end takes the end it prints inside (``činný do 1938``).  A
    company clause, or one dated ``od`` / ``po``, with no end at all is open-ended (B1);
    any other clause is a point in time.  An undated clause is no evidence until the
    model pass dates it (B11).  ``source_key`` is ``line_no.clause_no``, led by the
    ``ensemble_id`` for an ensemble's own chronicle.
    """
    if coded.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=["geo_id", "source", "source_key", "company_id"])
    C = coded[coded["start_lo"].notna() | coded["start_hi"].notna() | coded["end_hi"].notna()].copy()
    keep = (C["czech_activity"] | C["company"] | C[[c for c in EVENT_COLUMNS if c in C]].any(axis=1)
            | C["pause"] | C["puppet"])
    C = C[keep]
    no_end = C["end_lo"].isna() & C["end_hi"].isna()
    C.loc[no_end, "end_lo"] = C.loc[no_end, "end_inside"]
    C.loc[no_end, "end_hi"] = C.loc[no_end, "end_inside"]
    still_open = C["end_lo"].isna() & C["end_hi"].isna() & C["start_lo"].notna()
    C["open_end"] = still_open & (C["company"] | C["date_form"].isin(["from", "after"]))
    C["source"] = source
    C["source_key"] = C["line_no"].astype(int).astype(str) + "." + C["clause_no"].astype(int).astype(str)
    if "ensemble_id" in C:
        C["source_key"] = C["ensemble_id"].astype(int).astype(str) + "." + C["source_key"]
    return C


def _ensemble_chronicle_evidence(coded: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """An ensemble's own chronicle as evidence (D-145): like a place's, but about one company.

    Its company clauses carry that ensemble's ``company_id`` (no B2 matching); where the
    page lists decades, :func:`evidence_table` closes their open end with the company's.
    A German ensemble's clauses are German, never Czech activity.
    """
    C = _clause_evidence(coded, source="ensemble_chronicle")
    german = C["ensemble_german"].astype(bool)
    C.loc[german, "german"] = True
    C.loc[german, ["czech_activity", "company"]] = False
    C["company_id"] = [_ensemble_company_id(g, e) if c else pd.NA
                       for g, e, c in zip(C["geo_id"], C["ensemble_id"], C["company"])]
    return C


def _first_report_evidence(places: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The place page's *první zpráva*: activity certain in its year (B3)."""
    spans = [_span_from_precision(y, p) for y, p in
             zip(places["first_record_year"], places["first_record_precision"])]
    out = pd.DataFrame({"geo_id": places["geo_id"].astype(int), "source": "first_report",
                        "source_key": "", "start_lo": [s[0] for s in spans],
                        "start_hi": [s[1] for s in spans]})
    out["end_lo"] = out["end_hi"] = np.nan
    out["open_end"] = False
    out["czech_activity"] = True
    return out[out["start_lo"].notna()]


def _ends_agree(a_lo, a_hi, b_lo, b_hi, slack: int = MATCH_START_YEARS) -> bool:
    if pd.isna(a_lo) or pd.isna(b_lo):
        return True
    return a_lo - slack <= b_hi and b_lo - slack <= a_hi


def assign_companies(evidence: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """One ``company_id`` per company, across the ensemble list and the chronicle (B2).

    Within a place, a chronicle company clause joins the ensemble row whose start lies
    within :data:`MATCH_START_YEARS` and whose end does not contradict it — the closest
    start first, each ensemble row taken at most once, names not used.  The chronicle
    clauses left over join one another by the same rule, so ``1887 zal. SDO`` and
    ``1887-1934 SDO`` are one company.  Rows that are no company get <NA>.
    """
    company_id = pd.Series(pd.NA, index=evidence.index, dtype="string")
    companies = evidence[evidence["company"]]
    for geo_id, group in companies.groupby("geo_id"):
        anchors: list[tuple] = []          # (company_id, start_lo, end_lo, end_hi, from_ensemble, used)
        for idx, r in group[group["source"] == "ensemble"].iterrows():
            cid = f"{geo_id}:e{r['source_key']}"
            company_id[idx] = cid
            anchors.append([cid, r["start_lo"], r["end_lo"], r["end_hi"], True, False])
        clauses = group[group["source"] == "chronicle"].sort_values("start_lo", na_position="last")
        for idx, r in clauses.iterrows():
            best, best_gap = None, None
            for anchor in anchors:
                if anchor[4] and anchor[5]:
                    continue                    # an ensemble row already matched
                gap = abs(anchor[1] - r["start_lo"]) if pd.notna(r["start_lo"]) else np.inf
                if gap <= MATCH_START_YEARS and _ends_agree(anchor[2], anchor[3], r["end_lo"], r["end_hi"]):
                    if best_gap is None or gap < best_gap:
                        best, best_gap = anchor, gap
            if best is None:
                best = [f"{geo_id}:c{r['source_key']}", r["start_lo"], r["end_lo"], r["end_hi"], False, False]
                anchors.append(best)
            elif best[4]:
                best[5] = True
            company_id[idx] = best[0]
    return company_id


def evidence_table(places: pd.DataFrame, ensembles: pd.DataFrame, coded: pd.DataFrame,
                   pages: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
                   ensemble_coded: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Ensemble spans, chronicle clauses and first reports as one table of dated evidence.

    Key ``evidence_id`` (``source:geo_id:source_key``), asserted unique.  Every row has
    a start or an end interval.  Columns as :data:`EVIDENCE_COLUMNS`.  With the ensemble
    pages (``pages``, scraper step C) and their coded chronicles (``ensemble_coded``,
    :func:`code_clauses` of :func:`ensemble_chronicle_clauses`), sources
    ``ensemble_decade`` and ``ensemble_chronicle`` join, both under the ensemble's own
    ``company_id`` (D-145).
    """
    parts = [_ensemble_evidence(ensembles, pages), _clause_evidence(coded), _first_report_evidence(places)]
    if ensemble_coded is not None and len(ensemble_coded):
        assert pages is not None, "evidence: an ensemble chronicle needs its pages"
        parts.append(_ensemble_chronicle_evidence(ensemble_coded))
    ev = pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True, sort=False)
    preset = (ev["company_id"] if "company_id" in ev else pd.Series(pd.NA, index=ev.index)).astype("string")
    for column in EVIDENCE_COLUMNS:
        if column not in ev:
            ev[column] = np.nan
    flags = ["open_end", "hedged", "czech_activity", "company", "performance", "pause", "puppet",
             *[c for c in EVENT_COLUMNS if c not in ("performance", "attendance")], "attendance"]
    ev[flags] = ev[flags].astype("boolean").fillna(False).astype(bool)
    ev["titles"] = ev["titles"].fillna("")
    ev["evidence_id"] = ev["source"] + ":" + ev["geo_id"].astype(int).astype(str) + ":" + ev["source_key"]
    ev["company_id"] = preset.where(preset.notna(), assign_companies(ev))
    # D-145: a company whose page lists decades is possible in those decades only, so no
    # record of it — a place-chronicle clause matched to it by B2 included — stays open
    listed = ev.loc[ev["source"] == "ensemble_decade", "company_id"].dropna().unique()
    ev.loc[ev["company_id"].isin(listed), "open_end"] = False
    ev = ev[EVIDENCE_COLUMNS]
    assert ev["evidence_id"].is_unique, "evidence: key not unique"
    assert (ev[["start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi"]].notna().any(axis=1)).all()
    return ev


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The place × year panel
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def year_bounds(start_lo, start_hi, end_lo, end_hi, open_end: bool, hedged: bool,
                last_year: int = PANEL_LAST_YEAR) -> tuple[tuple | None, tuple | None]:
    """The years a record makes theatre *certain* and *possible*, as closed ranges or None.

    A span with an end is certain from its latest possible start to its earliest
    possible end, and possible over its whole width.  Open-ended (B1): certain only in a
    start year printed exactly, possible from there to ``last_year``.  A point is certain
    only when printed to the year; a decade or a ``kolem`` is possible across its width
    and certain in none (B10).  Known only by its end (``do 1910``): possible in the end
    year, certain in none.  Hedged (B4): never certain.
    """
    has_start = not pd.isna(start_lo) or not pd.isna(start_hi)
    has_end = not pd.isna(end_lo) or not pd.isna(end_hi)
    if not has_start:
        if not has_end:
            return None, None
        lo, hi = (end_lo if not pd.isna(end_lo) else end_hi), (end_hi if not pd.isna(end_hi) else end_lo)
        return None, (int(lo), int(hi))
    s_lo = start_lo if not pd.isna(start_lo) else start_hi
    s_hi = start_hi if not pd.isna(start_hi) else start_lo
    if has_end:
        e_lo = end_lo if not pd.isna(end_lo) else end_hi
        e_hi = end_hi if not pd.isna(end_hi) else end_lo
        certain = (int(s_hi), int(e_lo)) if s_hi <= e_lo else None
        possible = (int(s_lo), int(max(e_hi, s_hi)))
    elif open_end:
        certain = (int(s_lo), int(s_lo)) if s_lo == s_hi else None
        possible = (int(s_lo), max(int(s_hi), last_year))
    else:
        certain = (int(s_lo), int(s_lo)) if s_lo == s_hi else None
        possible = (int(s_lo), int(s_hi))
    return (None if hedged else certain), possible


PANEL_KEY = ["geo_id", "year"]


def place_year_panel(evidence: pd.DataFrame, geo_ids, first_year: int = PANEL_FIRST_YEAR,
                     last_year: int = PANEL_LAST_YEAR) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Every place × year, ``first_year``–``last_year``: Czech amateur theatre, certain and possible.

    Balanced: one row per place of ``geo_ids`` and year, key ``(geo_id, year)`` asserted.
    Columns, each ``_certain`` and ``_possible``:
    ``any_activity`` (some Czech-activity record, the first report included, B3);
    ``ensembles_active`` (distinct companies whose span covers the year);
    ``performances_min`` (certain: performance records printed to one year, each counting
    the number it states or 1; possible: records whose interval covers the year); one
    count per :data:`EVENT_COLUMNS` (German, bilingual and Latin are
    counted, never activity, B8).  Also ``performances_period_avg`` (a count stated over
    a span, ``1883-1910 173 her``, spread evenly over its certain years — an average, so
    kept apart from the minimum), ``plays_distinct_certain``, ``attendance_max``
    (largest audience stated in a record certain in the year), and
    ``activity_decade_certain`` (Czech activity certainly inside this year's decade, B10).
    A recorded pause (B12) turns certain activity and companies into possible for its
    certain years.  Puppet theatre is ``puppet_*`` only.
